A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hummingbird study and contain complete main text and Appendices A-R. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments and ablations in Section 5, plus additional evaluations, a 70-participant user study, and seed analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 1-3 and the user study in Appendix I, Table 10.

M1.justification: The SDXL/LoRA pipeline, MLLM context descriptor, BLIP-2 QFormer evaluator, two rewards, and inference procedure are unchanged in Section 4, Algorithm 1, and Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both retain VQAv2/GQA training, MME Perception, Bongard-HOI, ImageNet and its OOD variants, and the MME Artwork and Commonsense Reasoning evaluations in Appendices F-G. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same comparator membership, including RandAugment, Image Variation, Image Translation, Textual Inversion, and I2T2I SDXL. The controls, user-study comparator, and CLIP evaluator ablation are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The TTA/TPT procedures, data splits, metrics, model configurations, and training settings are unchanged. Appendix protocols also match, including the 50-question, 70-participant user study and GPT-4o fidelity evaluation.

E4.justification: Both contain the same reward, descriptor, fine-tuning, prompt-template, and evaluator ablations. OOD tests, failure examples, seed-sensitivity analysis, and convergence curves are likewise unchanged.

E5.justification: Both specify 20 generation seeds for diversity evaluation and retain the 10-100 seed analysis in Appendix K. Appendix P still reports averages over unspecified multiple runs; no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1-12 and the plotted and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Hummingbird's Bongard-HOI TPT average remains 68.73% in Table 2, and its user-study average remains 76.06% in Table 10.

T1.justification: Sections 3-4 and Appendix L retain the same definitions, reward and loss formulations, gradient expression, and mutual-information argument. No mathematical reasoning or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same novelty, fidelity-diversity, and benchmark-performance claims. The added project-page line does not alter their scientific meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including SDXL's symbolic-reasoning limitations, errors from MLLM context descriptions, the single-attribute focus, and the FID versus diversity discussion in Appendices A-B and H.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page URL after the abstract, providing an access pointer absent from v1. Implementation details in Section 5.2 and Appendix Q are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same works and research positioning. The introduction removes one redundant Feng et al. (2023) citation, but that work remains cited and discussed under Image Variation in Section 2.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short acknowledgments section describing the Microsoft internship and NSF support, adds the project-page line, and slightly shortens an introduction phrase and citation list. The main narrative and appendix structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The added project-page line and acknowledgments cause limited text reflow on pages 1-2 and 11-13, and the arXiv margin stamp changes. All 12 tables, 18 figures, and appendix-page layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new project-page pointer and explicit funding acknowledgment provide a small improvement in navigation and disclosure. The method, empirical evidence, mathematical content, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, so the benefit is limited to documentation.
